evidence.excerpt: Three genotyping methods were benchmarked for their ability to discriminate between a production strain and spontaneous variants arising during fermentation of Bacillus subtilis for surfactin production. Thirty isolates from production seed banks at three facilities, along with 12 laboratory-generated spontaneous variants, were characterised. RAPD-PCR resolved clusters at the facility level but failed to separate closely related spontaneous variants in 4 of 12 cases. AFLP provided higher resolution but required two working days per sample set. Whole-genome SNP calling from Illumina short reads correctly identified all variants and provided information on the location and predicted functional impact of mutations. Sequencing cost per isolate was estimated at €38 in 2017 prices in a batch of 24 samples, already competitive with AFLP for batches above 16 isolates. Practical recommendations for selecting the appropriate method based on facility throughput and technical capacity are provided.
